target: मैंने दो बार फ़ोन किया, फिर भी उसने नहीं उठाया।
english: I called twice, still he didn't pick up.
reason: Motto-like/moralising narrative ('she did not lose courage') – reads like a textbook uplift line, not something anyone says. Replacement keeps the same फिर भी (still/even so) connective in an ordinary complaint.

target: मेरी सीट बारह नंबर के डिब्बे में है।
english: My seat is in coach number twelve.
reason: Pointless trivia – nobody describes a train as 'a twelve-coach express'. Replacement keeps the same counting/number-with-noun point in a sentence a traveller actually uses.

target: हमारे यहाँ लोग हाथ जोड़कर नमस्ते करते हैं।
english: Where I'm from, people greet with folded hands.
reason: Meta/textbook trivia card ('Punjabi people greet like this') – it explains a fact rather than being usable speech. Replacement keeps the -कर participle + habitual present and is something a learner can genuinely say.

target: यहाँ से हवाई अड्डे तक कैसे जाएँ?
english: How do I get to the airport from here?
reason: Ungrammatical/stilted: हवाई अड्डा needs the oblique (हवाई अड्डे) before जाएँ. Same subjunctive direction-asking question, fixed to natural form.

target: बाहर जाते समय दरवाज़ा बंद कर देना।
english: Close the door when you go out.
reason: Classroom meta-instruction about writing word order – teaches about the language instead of being usable speech. Replacement keeps the -ते समय (while doing) structure plus an imperative.
Unnatural – 'Thursday is coming' is not something a Hindi speaker says. Replacement keeps the same basic X है pattern with a day name.

target: यह कुर्सी बैठने के लिए बहुत आरामदायक है।
english: This chair is very comfortable to sit in.
reason: Preachy health-advice line ('sitting with a straight back is good for health'). Replacement keeps the infinitive + के लिए + predicate adjective pattern in an everyday remark.
